newsitem.title: USA: N.J. JUDGE REJECTS PETITION STAY ON PENSION BOND SALE.
newsitem.headline: N.J. JUDGE REJECTS PETITION STAY ON PENSION BOND SALE.

text.p: - A New Jersey Superior Court judge Monday rejected a petition for a temporary stay on the state's pension bond sale.
The sale is expected Wednesday through a syndicate headed by Merrill Lynch & Co.
Alan J. Karcher, a lawyer for Mayor George Spadoro of Edison Township, asked for the temporary injunction while he appealed Phillip Carchman's earlier ruling upholding the sale.

Karcher argued that the proposal -- to raise $2.75 billion to liquidate state unfunded pension obligations by selling bonds -- does not meet two criteria the state Supreme Court laid out for exceptions to the state constitution's debt limitation clause.
Otherwise the state first must obtain voter approval in a referendum.

The pension bond law authorizes the state treasurer to contract with the nominally independent Economic Development Authority to sell the bonds in return for the pledge to pay the debt service from annual appropriations. It also helps balance the annual budget.

Gov. Christie Whitman's original pension bond plan was to borrow $3.4 billion enabling her to forgo $647 million in contributions to the state's four funds. The state Senate pared it and reduced its budget benefit to $590 million. --U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1650
